full_judgment:
2. Short facts leading to this revisional application is that Title Suit No. 206 of 1970 was decreed and the same was put to' execution in Execution Case No.8 of 1988. The plaintiff-opposite party, Muslima Khatun on coming to know about the said decree, filed a suit being Title Suit No. 147 of 1988 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, Second Court, Sylhet which is now pending for setting aside the decree in the aforesaid T.S. No. 206 of 1970. The plaintiff opposite party' alleged that she was not made a party in the previous Title Suit No. 206 of 1970 and that she being a widow of Late Abdus Sobhan has been in peaceful possession of the suit land, was threatened for eviction through the process of the Court. She filed an application under Order 39, rule I of the Civil Procedure Code on 25.9.1988 for restraining the defendant-petitioner from interfering with her possession till the disposal of the said suit. A show cause notice with ad-interim order of injunction was issued upon the defendant petitioners on 26.9.1988. The defendant petitioner filed written objection against temporary injunction. Upon hearing petitioners and the opposite parties, the learned Judge passed the order making the earlier order of ad interim injunction dated 26.9.1988 absolute by his order dated 23.1.1989. 

 3. Mr. Azizur Rahman Chowdhury, the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff opposite party, raised a preliminary point as to the maintainability of the present revisional application filed by the defendant-petitioners. Mr. Chowdhury argues that the application under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure is not maintainable inasmuch as the order under Order 39, rule I, being an appealable order, no revision lies thereto under law. 

 4. Let us see what is meant by 'preliminary point'. The expression 'preliminary' in Order XLI, r.23, of the Civil Procedure Code is not confined to such legal points only as may be pleaded as a bar to a suit but comprehends all points or issues of fact or law, determination of which has precluded the necessity for determining other points or issues which have, therefore, been, left undetermined." In the case of Mst. Jit Kuar Vs. Kehar Singh, AIR 1951 Pepsu page 130, it has been defined, "A preliminary point means a point, the decision of which is sufficient to dispose of the whole suit without the necessity of deciding other points involved in the case. It may be of fact or law. It would include a point which relates to the cause of action for the plaintiff or his locus standi to bring the particular suit. "Moreover, Order XLIV, rule 2, C.P.0 invests the Court with the discretion to dispose of the issues of law first leaving the issues of fact postponed. 

 6. From a bare reading of the judgment, it appears that the application filed by the plaintiff opposite party is an application under Order 39, rule I of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 9. It is further stated in the judgment," the plaintiff Opposite party filed the suit for declaration of Title that the decree obtained in Title Suit No. 206 of 1970 is fraudulent and inoperative and also prayed for a separate saham of 4 gondas share of the suit property. She also prayed for temporary injunction so that by putting the decree in execution she may not be evicted from the suit property till the disposal of the said suit." 

 10. Mr. J.N. Deb argues that plaintiff-Opposite party filed a petition for temporary injunction on 25.9.1988 which was rejected as the same was not moved. On the same date the plaintiff opposite party filed another petition under section 151 of the Civil Procedure Code for vacating the order of rejection and to allow the plaintiff opposite parities to move the petition. The petition was put up on 26.9.1988 and the same was heard in presence of the learned lawyers for both sides. The Court was pleased to issue show cause notice upon the defendant-petitioners and granted ad-interim injunction. Thereafter the defendant petitioner filed a written objection. The matter was heard and finally disposed of by order dated 23.1.1989 confirming the earlier order of ad-interim injunction passed on 26.9.1988. 

 11. The learned Judge observed "under the circumstances the plaintiff has filed this petition for temporary injunction so that defendant Nos. 27 and 28 may not dispossess her from the suit property by putting the Execution Case No. 8 of 1988 arising out of decree of the T.S No. 206 of 1970." 

 12. After considering the prima facie case of the plaintiff on the basis of materials submitted be-fore him and finding the balance of convenience and inconvenience in favour of the plaintiff, the learned judge allowed the petition on contest for temporary injunction restraining defendant Nos. 27 and 28 and confirmed the ad-interim order of injunction passed on 26.9.1988. 

 17. Now, therefore, turning to the merit of the case, it is to be looked into whether the order dated 23.1.1989 suffers from any error of law causing any error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The plaintiff opposite party's simple case is that she is a widow of late Abdus Sobhan and that she has a share in the property left by late Abdus Sobhan. That the defendant petitioner by practising fraud obtained a decree in Title Suit No. 206 of 1970 and that Execution Case No. 8 of 1988 has been started and on realising that she would be evicted by police force, she took the shelter of the court of law to protect her right, title and interest in the property. The defendant petitioners filed written objection against granting of temporary injunction and also filed a few papers in support of their cases. The defendant petitioners disowned the plaintiff opposite party as the wife of late Abdus Sobhan. They assert that Abdus Sobhan had divorced her. But the defendant petitioners could not show any Talaknama before the court in support of such claim. The learned Subordinate Judge considered the material papers filed by the par- ties in support of their respective cases. The defendant petitioners in support of their case placed a Photostat copy of notice of divorce and two receipts of notices served upon the Union Council Chairman and also receipts showing that the dowry was given to plaintiff opposite party. The learned Subordinate Judge considered these papers but could not accept the same as those receipts and papers were not legally proved and there is serious risk for the plaintiff to be likely prejudiced and therefore no reliance could be given thereto. On the other hand, the plaintiff opposite party filed photostat copies of some deeds of sale by the plaintiff-opposite party which she along with another daughter of late Abdus Sobhan had transferred by way of sale. Furthermore, in C.R. Case No. 427 of 1979 the -defendant-petitioners made the plaintiff-opposite party, Muslima Khatun, as opposite party No. 10, showing her to be the wife of late Abdus Sobhan. Moreover, plaintiff on oath had made the statement that she was the wife of late Abdus Sobhan. Upon consideration of these papers and averment, the court found a prima facie case in favour of plaintiff-opposite party and also found balance of convenience and inconvenience in her favour. He also appears to have found that she was threatened by some impending danger of being evicted from the suit land if the Title Execution Case No.8 of 1988 be allowed to be put into execution. The Court passed the order dated 23.1.1989 allowing temporary injunction by confirming the earlier order of ad-interim injunction dated 26.9.1988 to protect the right, title and interest of the plaintiff during the pendency of the Title Suit No. 147 of 1988 filed by her.
